lab_title: Structural Anatomy and Blood Flow of the Human Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers, four valves, and major vessels of the human heart in 3D space.
Trace the sequence of blood flow through the heart, accurately distinguishing between the oxygenated and deoxygenated pathways.
Relate the structural differences of the myocardium (right vs. left ventricle) to their functional roles in pulmonary and systemic circulation.
Explain the anatomical mechanism of the heart valves in preventing backflow and maintaining unidirectional blood flow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Orient students to the external anatomy of the heart and the major blood vessels that enter and exit the organ.
key_visuals: A life-sized, high-fidelity 3D model of a human heart suspended in the AR workspace.
Highlights on the superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, pulmonary veins, and the aorta.
student_actions: Rotate and scale the 3D heart model to view it from anterior, posterior, and lateral perspectives.
Select and correctly label the major vessels (SVC, IVC, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta) using a virtual laser pointer.

scenes.brief_purpose: Reveal the internal macroscopic anatomy of the heart, focusing on the spatial relationships and identification of the four chambers.
key_visuals: An animated coronal cross-section of the heart that opens to reveal the internal chambers.
Distinct color-coded shading for the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
student_actions: Interact with a sliding UI to open and close the coronal section of the heart.
Identify the right and left atria and ventricles, noting their relative positions.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the relationship between structure and function by comparing the myocardial wall thickness of the right and left ventricles.
key_visuals: A close-up view focusing on the muscular walls (myocardium) of the ventricles, with a cross-sectional cut emphasizing the interventricular septum and free walls.
An interactive measurement tool and visual callouts comparing the thin right ventricular wall with the much thicker left ventricular wall.
student_actions: Use the virtual calipers to measure and compare the thickness of the right and left ventricular walls.
Answer an interactive prompt explaining why the left ventricle requires a thicker myocardium (systemic vs. pulmonary resistance).

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the location, structure, and function of the four heart valves in maintaining unidirectional blood flow.
key_visuals: A superior transverse view (with the atria removed) looking down at the fibrous skeleton and the four valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic).
A slow-motion animation showing the valves opening and snapping shut in pairs during the cardiac cycle.
student_actions: Manually scrub through a timeline of a single cardiac cycle to observe valve states.
Identify which valves are open and which are closed during ventricular systole (contraction) and diastole (relaxation).

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of deoxygenated blood through the right side of the heart (pulmonary circulation).
key_visuals: A semi-transparent heart model with blue, glowing particles representing deoxygenated blood.

Animated flow showing blood entering from the vena cavae, filling the right atrium, passing through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle, and exiting via the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
student_actions: Place sequential waypoints along the blood flow path in the correct anatomical order.
Observe how the closure of the tricuspid valve prevents backflow of the blue particles into the atrium during right ventricular contraction.

scenes.scene_name: The Systemic Circuit and Dual-Loop Flow
scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the pathway of oxygenated blood through the left side of the heart (systemic circulation) and observe the complete dual-loop system.
key_visuals: Red, glowing particles representing oxygenated blood returning from the lungs into the left atrium, passing through the mitral valve to the left ventricle, and exiting the aortic valve into the aorta.
A final, combined animation showing both blue and red particle flows occurring simultaneously, illustrating the synchronized dual-loop circulation.
student_actions: Drag and drop labels to sequence the flow of oxygenated blood through the left side of the heart.
Activate the 'Dual-Loop' visualization to watch the simultaneous contraction of the atria followed by the ventricles, driving both pulmonary and systemic flows together.
